overlay-bug.title: The copy falls apart up high
overlay-bug.caption: The technician’s two rows as curves. Low tones match; the higher the tone, the further the copy falls below the exchange.

analog.title: Analog and digital filters
analog.caption: An analog filter works on the voltage itself, every instant, and has a response at every frequency. A digital filter works on samples and stops at 4,000 Hz.

prototype.title: The exchange’s gain, past the wall
prototype.caption: The analog prototype: the exchange’s filter. It has a response far beyond 4,000 Hz, where your line cannot follow.

wrap-vs-squeeze.title: Wrap it, or squeeze it
wrap-vs-squeeze.caption: Wrapping lays the ruler round and round, so different frequencies share a spot. Squeezing bends it on once, so every frequency gets its own spot.

arctan.title: The shape of arctan
arctan.caption: Small inputs come back almost unchanged; big ones crowd under the ceiling.

warping.title: The warping curve
warping.caption: Read up from the analog axis to find where a frequency lands; read across from the digital axis to find what lands there.

arrows.title: An arrow and its mirror
arrows.caption: Add an arrow and its mirror and the up-down parts cancel. Subtract them and the left-right parts cancel.

two-radians.title: Two kinds of radian
two-radians.caption: Digital tones count turns per sample and stop at π. Analog frequencies count turns per second and never stop.

s-line.title: Climbing the analog ruler
s-line.caption: Walk up the ruler and read the size of H: it is the manual’s gain formula. At 3,400 Hz the bottom of H points straight up.

bilinear.title: The bilinear transform as a machine
bilinear.caption: One substitution turns a formula in s into five numbers you can run, sample by sample.

zplane.title: The script’s filter on the circle
zplane.caption: The double zero sits on 4,000 Hz, where infinity landed. The poles sit well inside the circle: the filter is stable.

prewarp.title: Prewarping: read the curve backward
prewarp.caption: Start where you want the cutoff to land, and read back to the analog frequency that lands there.

echo.title: The prewarped copy’s echo
echo.caption: The echo flips sign every sample because the new poles sit near the far left of the circle. Both pairs are inside it: stable.

squeezed-prototype.title: The prototype, squeezed onto the line
squeezed-prototype.caption: The whole nearly flat stretch of the prototype lands below 3,400 Hz. That is why the prewarped copy is flatter than the exchange.

overlay.title: Three curves, one pinned point
overlay.caption: Prewarping pins one point. Below it the prewarped copy is flatter than the exchange, above it steeper.
